chapters.title: The Journey's End
chapters.summary:
The Hero Party makes a triumphant return to the Royal Capital after vanquishing the Demon King. The party includes Himmel the Hero, Eisen the Warrior, Heiter the Priest, and Frieren the Mage. As the party members celebrate, they reminisce about their long ten-year adventure. However, Frieren, being an Elf, felt it was short, as time passes differently for elves. Nevertheless, all of them were glad to have been able to adventure together. At the same time, the party watches the Era Meteors occur, and they all vow to meet again to watch the meteor shower again fifty years later.
The next day, the party members go their separate ways, with Frieren going on a journey to acquire more magic. In her pursuit of magic, she travels far and wide, which finally leads her back to the Royal Capital five decades later. She finds Himmel to have grown very old. Meanwhile, Frieren herself does not look a day older. Together, they meet Eisen, who hasn't changed much appearance-wise, as he is a dwarf, and Heiter, who has also aged like Himmel as a fellow human. Together, the hero's party once more goes to see the Era Meteors in a location a week's walk from the capital. They venture through many places, reminding Himmel of the memories of days past, finally reaching the place where they witness the Era Meteors once again. Shortly afterward, Himmel passes away, seemingly content. At his funeral, Frieren begins to cry, unaware of the reason why, as she simply traveled with him for a mere ten years. She questions why she never thought about getting to know him more given the short length of a human's lifespan. After the funeral, the party disbands once more, and Frieren goes on a voyage to acquire magic while also deciding to get to know humans better as well.

chapters.title: The Priest's Lie
chapters.summary:
Twenty years after Himmel the Hero's passing, Frieren is lost in a forest in the Holy City of Strahl trying to find the home of Heiter. A young girl finds Frieren and takes her to her house where she meets Heiter, who is now very elderly. The young girl, whose name is Fern, turns out to be a war orphan from the Southern Lands adopted by Heiter. Frieren reveals that she came to repay Heiter before he died, but when Heiter requests Frieren to adopt Fern as her disciple, she refuses, saying she will only be a burden. Heiter then asks Frieren to instead decipher a grimoire that supposedly contains records of lost resurrection and immortality spells. Frieren states that it might take five or six years, and Heiter also asks Frieren to teach Fern some magic during that time. 
Four years pass, and Frieren deciphers most of the grimoire and trains Fern to a point that would take an average person ten years to reach. One day, Heiter collapses. Frieren tells Fern, who is training in the forest, to take a break and go stay by his side. Fern refuses, saying she has yet to strike down a high rock from a distance, which would prove that she is capable of surviving on her own. Fern remembers how when she was younger, she was about to commit suicide after losing her parents in the war. Heiter stopped her and told her it would be a waste for her to die, as all the beloved memories she made her with parents would disappear from the world as well. Fern expresses her determination to repay Heiter by learning how to survive on her own, and so Frieren lets her be. 
Some more time passes, and Fern finally manages to strike the rock. Frieren finishes deciphering the grimoire, finding that neither resurrection nor immortality were recorded within. Heiter reveals that he was aware of this, and he only asked Frieren to decipher the grimoire to buy enough time for Fern to reach a level where she could be Frieren's disciple. Frieren asks Heiter why he saved Fern, and he answers that Himmel would have done the same. In his final days, Heiter makes a few more memories with Fern before ultimately passing away. After his burial, Frieren pours alcohol over Heiter's grave, and together with Fern, she continues her journey to acquire more magic.

chapters.title: Blue-Moon Weed
chapters.summary: Twenty-six years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Turk Region. They have been doing simple jobs for strange magic as rewards such as helping out a pumpkin farmer with the harvest. They come upon a village whose herbalist lady asks them to clean a statue of the Hero Himmel, who once fought for the village when a monster attacked it. After cleaning it up, the herbalist thanks them, and thinks of planting some flowers around the statue to add more color. Frieren almost uses magic that can produce flower beds, but she stops and decides that a blue-moon weed flower would be best, although she has never seen it before, as it is the flower of Himmel's hometown. She asks the herbalist, who takes the duo back to her shop, and explains that long ago, all the flower fields within the forest were destroyed, and there has not been a sighting of blue-moon weed for several decades on the continent. Meanwhile, Fern tries to hide a couple of seed rats, which are harmful animals that eat seeds, in her cloak but gets caught by Frieren, so she returns it to the forest. The duo decides to look for some blue-moon weed, because if they are able to analyze a live specimen, they will acquire magic that will allow them to make the flowers bloom. Six months pass, and they still have not found any blue-moon weed. Although this is a trivial amount of time for Frieren, Fern starts becoming impatient. Alone, she goes to the herbalist and explains that Frieren should not be spending her time on something nonexistent. The herbalist gives her a pouch of seeds of a related species as a substitute and tells Fern to convey her feelings to Frieren. Fern talks to Frieren, who understands and says they will stop after a little more searching. At the same time, a seed rat steals the pouch of seeds and runs away. The duo pursues it and eventually reaches an abandoned watchtower where many seed rats can be seen. Frieren picks up a flower petal that was on the ground near it. She explains that seed rats hide their feed by burying it in a safe place, but they often forget where they hide them. Frieren flies up to the top of the watchtower, and finds a multitude of blue-moon weed flowers. She analyzes a specimen and plants the flowers around Himmel's statue. The herbalist thanks them, and Frieren and Fern continue their voyage.

chapters.title: The Mage's Secret
chapters.summary: Twenty-seven years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in Warm. Frieren decides they should split up to replenish supplies for their journey. However, Fern feels Frieren is hiding something from her, so she starts tailing her. Fern sees Frieren spend a lot of time in front of an accessory shop before buying something. After that, she goes to a bar and asks where she can find some desserts. She talks to some rough-looking adventurers and then heads back to the inn. Fern quickly finishes her shopping before also returning. Frieren decides that they should go eat some tasty food as it has been a while. Frieren tells Fern to choose whatever she wants as she has some secret savings. Fern asks what Frieren will have, but answers before her as she could already tell. This causes Frieren to recall a memory with the hero party where Himmel also guessed correctly what Frieren wanted to have. She apologizes to Fern, as she does not know a thing about her, and she hands her a gift for Fern's birthday, which is a hair ornament. Fern is delighted and she thanks Frieren. She tells Frieren that her attempts to get to know more about Fern give her overwhelming bliss. The next day, Frieren and Fern continue their voyage, with Fern now wearing her new hair ornament. She asks Frieren if there is some goal to their journey. She replies that it is just out of interest to gather magic, and also to retrace the steps she took with the Hero Party as much as possible before they fade away.

chapters.title: Killing Magic
chapters.summary: Twenty-seven years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Größe Forest. Frieren is training Fern on defensive magic. Defensive magic is powerful, but it burns a lot of mana. It is directly linked to their survival. After training Frieren and Fern arrive in a village. An elder villager takes them to the place where Qual, the Elder Sage of Corruption, was sealed. Qual is a demon that committed immeasurable atrocities on the land 80 years ago and the Hero Party sealed him away. Frieren came to eliminate him as the seal is going to be undone soon. They reach the place and Frieren decides to remove the seal the next day and dispose of Qual. Back at the village inn, Frieren explains to Fern that she sealed Qual because he was too powerful to beat. He developed Zoltraak, the first piercing magic in history, which could pierce all of mankind's defensive magics. The next day, Frieren undoes Qual's seal, and he fires Zoltraak at the duo. Fern easily blocks it with her defensive magic, making her comment that Zoltraak was just ordinary offensive magic. Frieren explains that Qual's magic was overly powerful, but in just a few years after his sealing, Zoltraak was analyzed and mankind was able to develop powerful defensive magics to defend against it. Qual is able to deduce that defensive magic is taxing on one's mana and fires a barrage of Zoltraak spells at them. However, Fern is still able to defend the duo as she has already witnessed this in training. Frieren fires Zoltraak at Qual, destroying him with his own magic. Frieren and Fern return to the village and the villagers show them their gratitude, and they continue their voyage.

chapters.title: New Year's Festival
chapters.summary:
[[File:Frieren and Fern observe the debris CH6.png|thumb|left|200px|Frieren and Fern inspecting the debris on the coast.]]
Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Granz Channel. A village elder requests them to clean up the coast from washed-up debris, rewarding them with a book by the Great Mage Flamme, albeit only a counterfeit. Frieren still accepts the request, and the duo is able to clean up the coast in time for the New Year's Festival. Together, they witness the breathtaking sunrise reflecting off the pristine sea, just as the other members of the Hero Party once did.

chapters.title: The Land Where Souls Rest
chapters.summary:
During a flashback of the Hero Party's visit at Eisen's home, Heiter sees a couple of graves, which are Eisen's family, and starts praying for them. Eisen believes that people turn to dust after they die, and Heiter states that they go to Heaven. He believes Heaven exists because it would be better that way. The rest of the Hero Party also starts praying for Eisen's family, including Eisen.
Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Bredt Region visiting Eisen's home. Frieren offers to help Eisen with anything, and he requests she help him search for the Great Mage Flamme's notes in the Voll Basin, which supposedly contain records of her having conversed with the dead. He wants to find them so Frieren can tell Himmel about how she wanted to get to know him better. They finally find a great tree engulfing some ruins, which are being protected by a powerful barrier. Frieren recalls a memory from a thousand years ago when her master Flamme planted the sapling, that would become a thousand year old tree. Flamme tells Frieren that one day she will make a grave mistake and want to get to know people more and to come back to the Voll Basin so that she can guide her. Frieren enters the ruins and finds the real notes of Flamme. They said that Flamme reached Aureole, or Heaven, and spoke with her former comrades there. It is revealed that Aureole is in Ende, where the Demon King's Castle is right now. Frieren and Fern decide to head to Aureole, the land where souls rest.

chapters.title: One One-Hundredth
chapters.summary: After finding Flamme's notes, Eisen, Frieren, and Fern take a carriage back to Eisen's home. While Frieren sleeps, Eisen and Fern converse about how Frieren is a good teacher. Eisen sees them off at the border of the Bredt Region and tells Frieren how her ten-year journey with the Hero Party has changed her.

chapters.title: Phantoms of the Dead
chapters.summary: Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Wille Region. They reach a village whose people are disappearing after going over the mountain pass, supposedly taken by ghosts. The next day, the duo investigates and finds out the Einsam, Phantom Demons,{{Note|While the Einsam are referred to as "Phantom Demons," they are considered monsters and do not fall under the category of the human-like demons evolved from monsters. The kanji of "demon" in "Phantom Demon" is "鬼" (''oni''), while the kanji for the evolved-from-monsters demons is "魔族" (''mazoku'').}} are causing the disappearances. Frieren and Fern find and defeat him, and continue their voyage towards Aureole.

chapters.title: Solar Dragon
chapters.summary: Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren and Fern are in the Riegel Canyon. They try to defeat a Solar Dragon to get the grimoire in its nest but fail. So they think it is best to get a vanguard, Stark, who is living in a village along the canyons and is also Eisen's disciple. They meet an old granny who takes them to Stark. Along the way, she tells them Stark came to the village three years ago and saved them from the Solar Dragon, which was attacking the village. They meet Stark and find out that he is a coward who only managed to save the village three years back because the dragon left. Frieren gives him one night to decide whether to help them or not. At night, Fern hears a loud sound and goes to check on Stark, who she finds to be training.

chapters.title: The Northern Checkpoint
chapters.summary:
Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in Waal. Entry to the Northern Lands has been prohibited because monster activity is brimming, so Frieren decides they can relax in Waal for the time being. Fern discovers that they might have to stay in the city for two years, so she and Stark try to find another passage to the north, but to no avail. Stark does not want to stay too long as he wants to experience a deplorable yet fun journey and share his tales with Eisen.
Fortunately, the Castellan of Waal finds out Frieren is present, and as thanks for her prior service to the city and in consideration of the plight of the Northern Lands, allows her party to pass through the barrier. With great fanfare, the trio continue their voyage into the north.

chapters.title: Liberation Festival
chapters.summary: Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are on the Eng Road. They travel with a merchant after clearing the road which had been blocked due to a landslide. When they reach the town, they find out the Liberation Festival is taking place the same night, which commemorates the day the Hero Party subjugated the demon that was oppressing the region. The townspeople celebrate by decorating the statues of the Hero Party. The merchant tells Frieren that it is on this day everyone remembers Himmel and his party, making her recall a memory of when Himmel told her he makes statues of himself and the party so that Frieren would not be alone in the future. They reach the town and see the statues decorated with flowers. The next day, the trio continues their voyage towards Heaven.

chapters.title: Monsters That Speak
chapters.summary: Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in Graf Granat's Domain. As the trio walks into town, Frieren senses some demons and tries to kill them, but she is stopped by the town's guards. The demons, led by Lord Lügner, are supposedly messengers of peace, but Frieren calls them incomprehensible wild beasts that mimic human voices. She is then thrown into the mansion dungeon. Fern and Stark investigate and find out Aura the Guillotine, a great demon who served the Demon King as one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, has requested peace after being long at war with the town. Frieren states that it is futile to negotiate with demons, as they only use words as a means of deception rather than communication. She decides to break out of the dungeon once the disorder starts. Meanwhile, Lügner wonders where he has seen Frieren before and smiles as she is the only one in town who knows the true nature of demons.

chapters.summary: Graf Granat leads Lügner to his son's room and is about to kill him as vengeance for his son. However, Granat empathizes with Lügner when he tells him that his father was also killed by humans in the ongoing human-demon conflict. Lügner reveals to Linie, the demon girl, that this is actually a lie in order to placate the Graf. He tells Linie that their true goal is to get the Graf to release the defensive barrier surrounding the town so that Aura the Guillotine's army can destroy it. Meanwhile, the demon boy, Draht, goes to the dungeon to try to assassinate Frieren. He fails, and she is able to kill him easily, remarking that this is one beast down.

chapters.title: The Murder of a Guard
chapters.summary: After Frieren kills Draht, she exits the dungeon and finds the guard dead. Meanwhile, Fern and Stark have lunch and decide to go appeal to Graf Granat for Frieren's release from prison so she can defeat Aura the Guillotine and her executioners. Meanwhile, Lügner finds out Draht was killed through Linie. Graf Granat confronts Lügner, and when Lügner's excuse falls apart, correctly suspects that Draht killed the guard. Now that his plan has failed, Lügner reveals his true colors and kills the guards and injures Graf Granat. He spares Granat's life so he can lift the protective barrier on the town. As Fern and Stark head to the Graf's estate, Fern spots Frieren stealthily walking while disguised. Frieren tells them what happened in the dungeon, and says that she will leave the town, leaving Fern and Stark to deal with the demons in town, despite Stark's pleas for her to help them. Frieren senses Aura in the distance and decides to quickly finish her off.

chapters.title: Frieren the Slayer
chapters.summary: After meeting with Frieren, Fern and Stark sneak into Graf Granat's mansion to rescue him. In the meantime, Lügner tries to get Graf Granat to tell him how the barrier magic works, but to no avail. He leaves the Graf to think over it carefully while trying to find a grimoire about it in his mansion. Stark enters the room and tries to free him, but Lügner and Linie return. Stark attacks Lügner but is unable to kill him. However, he gives an opening to Fern who was outside the window to shoot Lügner with magic. Stark and Fern escape with Graf Granat, and Lügner decides they will go after them as soon as he heals. Meanwhile, Frieren descends upon Aura's army.

chapters.title: The Undead Army
chapters.summary: After taking Graf Granat to safety, Stark and Fern tell the Graf that Frieren is innocent. The Graf agrees, telling them she and the Hero Party had protected the town from Aura before. Meanwhile, Frieren confronts Aura who surrounds her with her undead army. Granat reveals that Aura fights with a magic tool known as the Scales of Obedience which weighs Aura's mana against her opponent's. The one with greater mana is then given control over the other and cannot be fully resisted. In her five hundred years serving as one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, not once has Aura lost in a battle of mana. Frieren starts battling Aura's army using an anti-magic, as Himmel scolded her any in the past for blasting the army away. Aura asks why she would do so since Himmel is gone, which angers Frieren and results in her deciding to kill Aura without mercy.

chapters.title: Raid
chapters.summary: Stark and Fern leave Graf Granat at the church and decide to split up, Stark to find Frieren and Fern to evacuate the town's citizens. They are unexpectedly attacked by Lügner and Linie who separate them. After pinning Fern to a wall using blood magic, Lügner questions her about the whereabouts of Frieren whilst commenting that Stark will not receive a pleasant death. Meanwhile, Stark has engaged in a fight with Linie. After the initial surprise attack by Linie, Stark wonders why her technique is so similar to his Master's. While Lügner is distracted, Fern grabs her staff and breaks out of demon's hold. Lügner tells Fern that she would lose her head first if she attacked, for he has spent the greater part of his life dedicated to honing his magic. Fern remembers Frieren telling her that Fern's strength lies in her casting speed. She tells Lügner that she, too, has spent the greater part of her life dedicated to magic before blasting him with a large-scale spell.

chapters.title: Master's Technique
chapters.summary: Fern blasts Lügner, who only survives through reflexively defending his heart. The demon then responds with an attack of his own, purporting to crush Fern with his full strength. Meanwhile, Linie states that Stark has lost, but Stark stands up to continue fighting her. Lügner begins to lose ground against Fern and urges Linie to finish her fight. The demon initially appears to overwhelm Stark, but Stark remembers his Master's words and stands up again. He tanks a hit from Linie and uses the opening to slash her across the chest. In the midst of fighting Fern, Lügner's attention is drawn away by Linie's defeat. In his moment of distraction, he is blasted through the heart by Fern.

chapters.title: Coward
chapters.summary: After being struck by Fern, Lügner lays on the verge of death. He realizes that Frieren and Fern have been limiting their mana levels, a despicable and cowardly act. Fern concurs, then finishes Lügner off. The story then flashes back to Frieren's past, where she encounters Flamme after her village was destroyed by a demon. Flamme finds Frieren on the verge of death and decides to make Frieren her apprentice. The pair are accosted by Demon in pursuit of Frieren, who judge Flamme to be weak based on her mana and call for her to leave Frieren behind if she wishes to keep her life. Flamme calls the three demons arrogant and careless, before releasing her limited mana and destroying the Demon. After Frieren heals, Flamme teaches Frieren how to limit her mana, and tells her to keep up her mana limiting for her entire life to deceive Demon. The flashback ends with Frieren facing off against Aura. Aura's mana output is visibly greater than Frieren's, and Aura questions if it was the right call for Frieren to expend so much mana.

chapters.title: The Scales of Obedience
chapters.summary:
Frieren and Aura continue to face off against each other. Using her Scales of Obedience, Aura casts the Spell of Obedience: Auserlese. Frieren notes that based on her mana, Aura must have trained for most of her five hundred years of life. In a flashback, Frieren's training under Flamme's apprenticeship is shown. Flamme tells Frieren that demons cannot limit their mana because they are beholden to it as a form of status. All the while, Frieren continues to train in restricting her mana. She promises Flamme to keep a low profile until she has defeated the Demon King.
Once Flamme perishes due to old age, a series of scenes show Frieren's life, all while limiting her mana, up until she is recruited by the Hero Party and they face down the Demon King. The flashback then ends with Aura weighing Frieren's soul against her own. Initially, Aura seems assured in her victory, but slowly, the scale tips towards Frieren's side. Frieren tells Aura that she was limiting her mana and that Aura miscalculated, and when Aura reacts in disbelief, Frieren releases her full mana, which dwarf's Aura's mana. The scale tips fully to Frieren's side, and turning her back, Frieren commands Aura to kill herself, finally defeating the Sage of Destruction.

chapters.title: A Victory and a Funeral
chapters.summary: After Frieren defeats Aura, she reconvenes with Fern, Stark, and Graf Granat. Frieren tells Stark and Fern she is proud of them for defeating Lügner and Linie. Graf Granat inspects the now inanimate bodies of Aura's undead army, and thanks Frieren for minimizing the damage to the bodies and paying respect to the heroes of the Northern Lands. He then commands his subordinates to give the dead a proper burial. The trio then return to the Graf's mansion, where the Graf grants Frieren any reward within reason. Frieren asks for the grimoire of the Great Mage Flamme the Graf supposedly possesses, and though it is a fake, Frieren reveals she knew all along and is happy with it nonetheless. Frieren's Party then rest and relax in the city, joining in on the festivities and helping with rebuilding. Before they depart from the city, they, along with the other citizens of Graf Granat's Domain, pay respects to the fallen heroes of the Northern Lands who have at last been properly buried. After making final preparations to travel north, Frieren's Party head out of the city. Graf Granat sees them off until the gate and informs them that in order to head to Ende, the party will first need to go to Äußerst and receive a first-class mage certification with the Continental Magic Association. However, as soon as they begin their travels north, the party gets lost in the snow.

chapters.title: The Elves' Wish
chapters.summary: Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is in the Decke Region. Stark has collapsed and there is a heavy snowstorm so they seek shelter in an old cabin at the base of the Schwer Mountains. As they enter, they see an elf doing squats. Fern protests staying there and suggests finding another place as there is a pervert inside. Before they can leave, the elf opens the door and asks Frieren if she is also an elf. They head inside and the elf, who is a monk named Kraft, converses with Frieren about how long it has been since he encountered another elf and how he arrived in the cabin. As Stark rests in the cabin after being warmed up by Kraft, Frieren and Fern help Kraft carry food from his cart. Frieren's Party spends half a year in the cabin due to the dangerous weather. Close to spring, Kraft and Frieren discuss the Goddess of Creation. Kraft believes in the Goddess and Heaven as well as he wishes for someone to acknowledge his achievements. He then asks Frieren to tell him about herself so that he can praise her in the Goddess' place as she does not believe in the Goddess. This causes Frieren to remember how Heiter asked the same of her in the past and she declines Kraft's offer. Frieren's Party and Kraft part ways as they continue their separate adventures, with Kraft promising Frieren they will meet again.

chapters.title: The Village of the Sword
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is in the Schwer Mountains. The party presses towards the north and reaches the Village of the Sword, which protects the Sword of the Hero. The blade was pulled out by Himmel 80 years ago. The party members meet with the village chief, who tells Frieren that she didn't fulfill her vow of coming half-century later to fulfill her duty of exterminating the monsters that regularly appear around the village. The next day, the party kills numerous monsters that appear near the cave which surprisingly still holds the Sword of the Hero. It is revealed that Himmel was never able to pull the sword out, but the story was spread that he did so that the hero could be arbitrarily glorified by future generations. The village chief thanks Frieren's Party and they continue their voyage.

chapters.title: A Gift to a Warrior
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Appetit Region. On Stark's eighteenth birthday, Frieren and Fern discuss what to give him as birthday gifts. Frieren decides on a potion that melts clothes, which is quickly shut down by Fern, who pours it on her, leaving Frieren to find a new gift. Fern decides to investigate Stark on her own and ends up asking him directly what he desired. Stark mentions how he never received gifts growing up due to his weakness, and his brother, Stoltz, the best warrior in his hometown and the only one kind to Stark, was the one to fight against demons during an attack while he simply fled. Fern comforts him and they find a gift, returning to the inn where Frieren is cooking giant hamburger steaks. Frieren reveals she received the recipe from Eisen, who had always made steaks for Stark's birthday and for the members of the Hero Party during their journey as a way of expressing gratitude towards their efforts as warriors. Stark recalls his brother making a steak for his birthday as well and that his brother was the one who told him to escape the fateful night of the demon attack. In better spirits, he enjoys the rest of his birthday with his companions.

chapters.title: A Priest from an Ordinary Village
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren, Fern and Stark are in the Alt Woods. A man is stuck in a bottomless swamp, and he recounts the story of his childhood friend to Frieren in order to gain sympathy and ask for her help. Frieren uses magic to pull him out. The man walks with the party to his village and he invites them there, but they refuse as they wish to reach a major town, and they go on their way. On the way to the town, Stark gets bitten by a snake and the party heads back to the previous village to get him treated. The village's priest states that he is unable to cure Stark. However, his younger brother Sein, who is the man from before, enters upon them and recognizes Frieren's party, and immediately treats Stark with ease. The priest asks Frieren to take Sein away from the village, because he believes that Sein has always been searching for someone to support him to go on an adventure. Fern and Stark are in favour of having a priest in the party, but Frieren is unsure. Stark goes to invite Sein to join on his own. He finds Sein gambling, and Sein tells him that if Stark manages to beat him he will join them. When Fern and Frieren go to check on Stark, they find out that both he and Sein lost badly. Frieren tries to ask Sein to join them, but he refuses, saying he is too old and that it is too late now. This reminds her of how she used to be in the past and how Himmel managed to persuade her to join the Hero Party. She tries to convince Sein in the same way, and he seems to be inspired, but refuses again after contemplating a little. Frieren concludes that she truly does despise him, and that is why she chose to invite him to be a comrade regardless, a logic Sein fails to understand.

chapters.title: The Priest and His Regret
chapters.summary: Frieren's Party decides to stay in the village and attempts to recruit Sein nearly every day. After many attempts, Sein discloses the reason he doesn't intend to become an adventurer and track his best friend is that his friend told Sein that he would return in three years but ten years have passed since then, so he believes that his friend is already dead. However, after being confronted by Frieren, Sein eventually admits that the real reason why he cannot leave is that he cannot abandon his older brother, who also stayed in the village for Sein's sake when he was a child. This admission angers Sein's older brother, who slaps Sein and points out that he has not once regretted the decision he made, but Sein has. Sein apologizes to his older brother and decides to join the Frieren's Party after all in pursuit of his best friend.

chapters.title: Ideal Adult
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Raad Region. Fern and Stark fight after Fern becomes upset at Stark for not buying her a birthday present. The two eventually reconcile with Sein's guidance and proceed to shop for a gift for Fern together. Frieren tells Sein that Fern must have sought his guidance due to his resemblance to Heiter, who Sein believes to be an ideal adult unlike himself. Frieren proceeds to pat his head, as she believes that Sein is managing being a proper adult just fine.

chapters.title: Mirrored Lotus
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Bande Woods. The party catches a ride on a wagon. Frieren discusses the bracelet Stark bought Fern for her birthday, which shares the same mirrored-lotus flower design as a ring Himmel previously purchased for Frieren. Their discussion is interrupted by an attack from a bird-like monster, who lifts the wagon in the sky. Frieren jumps out of the wagon and blasts the monster in midair, dropping them to the ground and damaging the wagon in the process. While the party repairs the carriage, Frieren realizes she has lost Himmel's ring. Meanwhile, Sein reveals that the mirrored lotus represents eternal love in flower-language, much to Stark's dismay and Fern's annoyance. After the wagon is fixed, Fern realizes that Frieren has lost her ring and assists her in searching for it. With the aid of magic that seeks out lost accessories from the merchant, Frieren can locate the ring. As the party proceeds onwards through the woods, Frieren reflects on how she obtained the ring and that she is happy she did not give up on it.

chapters.title: Chaos Flower
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Laub Hills. Sein is complaining due to the lack of variety in party members. The party soon approaches a village, where they notice the villagers are all sleeping. As Sein examines them, he identifies that the villagers have been cursed by a monster. He asks the party to hurry as the easiest way to dispel the curse is to eliminate it. However, before they leave the village, Stark falls asleep as well, followed by Fern some time later. Sein and Frieren proceed onward, until Sein senses the presence of the monster. Hearing this, Frieren tells Sein to wake her when the monster appears before succumbing to the curse as well. Sein then proceeds to engage in a fight with the monster, a confusion flower that reflects magic. Having trouble against it, he decides to awaken Frieren, trusting in her words that she would defeat the monster, which she proceeds to blast with offensive magic. After awakening, the villagers thank the party, who proceed to head on their way.

chapters.title: The Orden Family
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren, Sein, Fern and Stark approach the Fortress City of Vorig. Right outside the city, Stark is noticed by a nobleman named Orden. Orden takes the party to his estate with a request for Stark. While Frieren initially refuses Orden's request, he offers to pay them for Stark's services, and with the party already running low on funds, she agrees to hear him out. Due to Stark's resemblance to Orden's deceased son Wirt, he wants Stark to impersonate his son as a way to boost morale. Stark is then taught in the ways of etiquette by the butler Gabel. After a bout of practice, Orden leads Stark to teach him the Orden Family's swordsmanship. As they head to the training grounds, they come across Orden's second son Mut. Orden criticizes Mut's weakness, reminding Stark of his own father, but he soon realizes Orden's relationship with Mut is different. After three months have passed, Stark attends the social gathering whilst posing as Orden's son and dances with Fern. Afterwards, Orden praises Stark's strength, but before he can even ask, Stark tells Orden that he is not a replacement for his son, and that he needs to return to his own foster father lest he regrets the words they parted on. Orden agrees, and the two part amicably. While Frieren picks out her grimoire, Stark notices Orden encouraging Mut in his training, and smiles knowing Orden won't have to worry about matters of a heir.

chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is in the Klar Region. They are traveling to meet one of Frieren's old friends, a dwarven warrior whom Frieren calls Old Man Voll. Frieren tells Stark to train with Voll and throughout the week, while the party completes tasks for the village, reminisces with Voll about the past. At the end of the week, Frieren thanks Voll for giving her the chance to get to know the Hero Party all those years ago. Voll asks if Frieren still remembers Himmel's face and voice, as despite his wife being his reason for protecting the village, he no longer recalls hers. The two continue reminiscing, and upon hearing that Frieren is currently traveling to Ende, Voll wishes for a peaceful era to arrive soon. Frieren does not correct him and instead tells him she will carry his memory with her. The next day, as Frieren's Party is about to depart, Voll tells them that he had a dream of his wife. The party then continues their journey north.

chapters.title: The Statues of Heroes
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is traveling along the Rohr Road. Sein stops to talk to a farmer, and reminds the party that his reason for journeying is to reunite with his best friend. The friend's name is Warrior Gorilla, while Sein's nickname is Priest Goatee. They stop by a town before the road forks off into several paths where Sein asks about Gorilla. He is directed to a granny who was close to Gorilla, but she makes the party help with several errands before she tells them anything. The final errand is polishing a statue of some forgotten heroes that look like Sein and Gorilla, but Frieren realizes the Gorilla lookalike is Kraft. Sein, now knowing one of the forgotten hero's names, recalls standing with Warrior Gorilla next to a statue of the same forgotten heroes with Heiter. Gorilla vows to be a hero that is remembered like Himmel and dubs himself Warrior Gorilla, as to not be forgotten, a hero must have an unforgettable name. In response, Heiter gives Sein the nickname Priest Goatee, claiming he will one day match the other forgotten hero. As Sein and co finish polishing the statue, the granny tells them that Warrior Gorilla headed towards Tür, which is the opposite direction of where Frieren's Party is headed and leaves Sein unsure of what to do.

chapters.title: A Reason to Begin the Journey
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Frieren's Party is on the Rohr Road. They are discussing Warrior Gorilla's whereabouts, which are likely in the opposite direction from Äußerst. Finding Warrior Gorilla was Sein's reason for going on a journey, so this complicates things. They decide to put off the decision of what Sein will do until tomorrow, and they then go to a cabin Stark rented. While getting supplies, Fern notes that her hands are chilly, to which Frieren says it's because it's gotten colder lately. They attempt to continue their journey the next day, but a cold wave that is estimated to last for about a month stops them, meaning the party must stay in the village for a bit longer. Around the end of the cold wave, Frieren calls on Sein to mediate between Fern and Stark again, which leads to Stark apologizing to Fern. Afterward, Frieren and Sein are having a drink in a tavern, which leads to Sein asking Frieren why she was so concerned about him to the point where she told him to go on a journey with them. Frieren replies that it's because he reminded her of her old self before she joined the Hero Party and subjugated the Demon King. She adds that it is what Himmel would have done, and that the Hero Party gave her the courage to travel and taught her to understand how fun it is to travel with comrades. Sein agrees that the journey has been fun. Afterwards, when the cold wave is over, Frieren's Party departs for Äußerst, although without Sein, who has chosen to pursue Warrior Gorilla in order to not bear anymore regrets. The now separate parties continue their journeys.

chapters.title: Emotional Support
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after Himmel the Hero's passing, Frieren's Party arrive in the Offen Mountain Range. Stark walks back to their camp, where Frieren is asleep, and he is surprised to see that Fern is also still sleeping. He prepares their food, and when he tries to wake Fern up, he notices she seems unwell. He wakes up Frieren so she can check on Fern, and Frieren deduces that Fern has a fever. Frieren uses notes left by Sein for treating illnesses and diagnoses Fern using magic, concluding that she has a cold, and she and Stark move Fern to a nearby cabin. Frieren comforts Fern by holding her hand like she did when she was ill as a child, much to Fern's embarrassment, and Frieren and Stark subsequently depart to search for herbs. On their way, Frieren comments that Fern will be an adult soon, and she still views Fern as a child in her heart. They arrive at an Icicle Cherry Blossom tree, and Stark asks Frieren why she held Fern's hand, as she never treated Fern like a child to that extent before. Frieren asks Stark what she should have done, and he tells her that she should just do what her heart tells her to, as some individuals need emotional support. His words remind Frieren of Himmel holding her hand when she was sick, just like she did with Fern. Frieren extracts the mushroom growing at the base of the tree and prepares the medicine, which she gives to Fern, eventually leading to her recovery. With Fern's improved condition, Frieren and her party depart to continue on their journey.

chapters.title: The First-Class Exam
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in the Kühl Region. The trio spot Äußerst in the distance and catch a coach the rest of the way. Meanwhile, in a remote area of Graf Granat's Domain, Mage Übel meets Monk Kraft when accosted by thieves. Übel reveals that she intends to take the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst and the two part ways. Some time later, at the Northern Branch of the Continental Magic Association in Äußerst, Frieren and Fern are informed the First-Class Mage Exam will be held in two months. Despite not having received the necessary mage class standing necessary to partake in the exam, an older mage recognizes Frieren's Holy Emblem and allows her to participate. Frieren and Fern then spend the next two months training for the exam. Two months later, all the mages participating in the First-Class Mage Exam have gathered. The proctor of the first exam, Genau, commences the first exam, a team battle, by splitting the examinees into groups of three. Frieren and Fern both find their teammates. To Frieren's dismay, her teammates are already fighting amongst themselves.

chapters.title: Stille—Meteoric Iron Bird
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Frieren and Fern are in the Grobe Basin, the location of the first stage of the first-class mage examination. Genau explains the exact rules of the first stage. First, each party must possess a cage with a bird native to the area, the "meteoric iron bird" called the "Stille", by sunset the next day. Secondly, all party members must be present and cannot leave the boundaries of the examination area, which has been demarcated with an impenetrable barrier spell. After explaining the rules, the exam commences. Frieren's teammates introduce themselves as Lawine and Kanne. Lawine spots a Stille in the middle of a lake, and though Kanne and Lawine coordinate their magic perfectly, it easily escapes. They proceed to observe more Stilles for the rest of the day. That night, Kanne is attacked by a bird monster but saved by Frieren who appears and restrains the monster. Frieren asks Kanne about her relationship with Lawine. Kanne recalls her first time learning flight magic and tells Frieren that Lawine is the one who showed her how to overcome frightening things. This causes Frieren to remember a moment with the Hero Party and Heiter's words that adventurers overcome their fear in different ways. Kanne then points out something that may help them catch a Stille. Meanwhile, Fern returns to her party, having already captured a Stille, and Übel indicates that the first stage will soon turn into a battle royale.

chapters.title: Commence Capture Strategy
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Frieren, Lawine, and Kanne are discussing their observations from Stille-watching. Frieren reveals she knows a spell that captures a bird that can assist in capturing a Stille and decides on a strategy for their team. Meanwhile, Fern, Übel, and Land realize that the barrier around the exam grounds is keeping out the river water, causing most of the water in the Grobe Basin to gather in the lake in the center of the exam grounds. This will cause Stilles and examinees alike to flock to the lake. The Fourth Party elects to avoid in lake in hopes of avoiding battle, but their hopes are dashed when Wirbel's team attacks them. Before a battle can break out, they are interrupted by a burst of magic from the lake courtesy of Lawine, who has frozen over the entire lake. While other parties attempt to melt the lake, Denken infers that it is a wasted effort as the usage of so much mana will deter any other Stilles from showing up. Denken then decides their party will steal the Second Party's Stille, and Wirbel's party and Fern's party begin to battle. Meanwhile, the Second Party continues to enact their strategy around the forest.

chapters.title: A Spell to Capture a Bird
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, the Thirteenth Party, which consists of Denken, Richter, and Laufen, moves to dismantle the Second Party's elaborate plan. The Thirteenth Party notes how inexperienced many of the examinees are. Richter states the exam is so dangerous because the Continental Magic Association wants to foster strong first-class mages, but Denken disagrees with this ideology as he values authority over strength. The different teams are shown all attempting to obtain a Stille in their own ways. Denken notes that every body of water they come across has faint traces of mana circulating through it. He deduces that there is one body of water the Second Party has not tampered with, and their whereabouts must be nearby it. Meanwhile, Frieren completely suppresses her mana and sits in wait for a Stille. Finally, after significant time has passed, a Stille lands on her shoulder, and Frieren uses her bird-capturing magic. This reveals her position to the Thirteenth Party, and Laufen quickly uses her magic to intercept the Second Party before they can escape.

chapters.title: Time for Resolve
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Fern and Wirbel's teams continue to fight. Fern faces off against Ehre, who declares that if Fern were facing off against Wirbel, she would be dead. Fern finds this curious, as she feels Ehre is the strongest among her party. Ehre refutes this and says that Wirbel's experience is on an entirely different level and as such, Übel is likely to be killed. Fern appears unconcerned and fires a swarm of offensive magic that overwhelms Ehre's defenses. Meanwhile, Übel fights against Wirbel using her cleaving magic. Though both manage to figure out the weaknesses of their opponents' magic, after a brief fight where Übel is able to slash Wirbel's face, Wirbel is able to immobilize Übel using Sorganeil, the spell of binding. Wirbel notes that Übel had aimed for his eyes instead of his neck and in his experience, this marked her as a degenerate who enjoyed killing. He muses that it would be better to kill Übel on the spot. Übel buys time by asking about Wirbel's history. Wirbel reveals that his magic allows him time to build up the resolve to kill, but in the end he has never shirked from a necessary kill; as he speaks, he raises his staff to Übel's head. However, he is stopped by Fern, who sneaks up behind him and holds Wirbel at staff point. As the three of them are now at an impasse, Fern proposes that they strike a deal.

chapters.title: A Reason to Fight
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Wirbel asks what happened to Ehre. Fern, expressionless, tells Wirbel that she killed Ehre. Since one of the conditions to pass is for all party members to be present, Wirbel concedes defeat and leaves. Removed from the rest of their parties, Land is still fighting Scharf, who controls flower petals to slice and disable Land's dominant arm. As he prepares to behead Land, Land notes that Scharf is bad at mana detection. Another figure of Land appears behind Scharf, paralyzing him, and Land reveals that he has been using a clone of himself since the beginning of the exam. Wirbel comes across Ehre lying in the middle of a clearing and realizes Fern's deception, but Ehre and Scharf are both unable to move. Believing they will fail for sure, Wirbel carries them both around the exam grounds and reminisces on his motivation to fight. By chance, they happen across a Stille perched in a tree which Wirbel summarily paralyzes with Sorganeil. Meanwhile, the Thirteenth Party has found the Second Party, with Laufen confronting the three mages in the Second Party alone. Laufen disappears and uses magic to steal the Stille away from Frieren in the blink of an eye, leaving the Second Party to figure out where Laufen has gone.

chapters.title: Privilege
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Laufen escapes with the stolen Stille using her magic. At the same time, at a high vantage point within the barrier, Genau takes tea with the proctor of the second exam, Sense. Genau believes luck and strength to be important qualities for mages to possess, and he and Sense argue over their philosophies for exams. Meanwhile, Denken and Richter move to fight the Second Party. Denken recognizes that Frieren is the Mage of the Hero Party and wishes to challenge her. Richter is surprised that Denken is not after the "privilege" bestowed by the Great Mage Serie, who can grant any magic that one desires, but states nonetheless that he will kill Lawine and Kanne. However, Denken tells him that will not be necessary as he will crush Frieren. Richter then separates the battlefield using earth manipulation magic, and the Second and Thirteenth Parties prepare to face off. Alone with Frieren, Denken says that the pursuit of magic is what brings the greatest joy, which reminds Frieren of a previous meeting with Serie where Frieren rejected Serie's "privilege" for the same reason. This lead Flamme to declare that Frieren, as a mage of a peaceful era, would be able to defeat the Demon King. Reminded of her master's words, Frieren affirms that the joy of pursuing magic is what it truly means to be a mage.

chapters.title: Recapture the Stille
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Lawine and Kanne begin to fight Richter in a battle of attrition. However, Richter utilizes the flaw in defense magic, its weakness against physical mass, and using his earth manipulation magic and greater mana, easily overwhelms Lawine and Kanne. Richter calls out Lawine's bluff about manipulating the water within his body, correctly guessing that neither Lawine nor Kanne would be able to visualize such magic, and tells the pair to settle down while Denken defeats Frieren. Denken uses a powerful series of spells that impresses even Genau and Sense, the latter of whom calls into question the integrity of the exam ground's barrier, but Genau states that as it is cast by the Great Mage Serie, the barrier is impenetrable. Though Denken casts more spells, Frieren is able to slip past his defenses and defeat him using basic offense magic. She then threatens Denken's life to draw out Laufen, and after restraining both Laufen and Denken to a tree, recovers the Stille. Seeing that Denken has lost, Richter prepares to face Lawine and Kanne seriously. Despite Denken's concern for Lawine and Kanne's safety, Frieren is assured that they will win, and indicates that she has finished deciphering Serie's barrier.

chapters.title: Water-Manipulation Magic
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Richter begins to seriously fight Lawine and Kanne. Frieren casts a spell, and though Genau states that it is impossible, manages to shatter Serie's barrier. This catches Serie's attention, as she has been waiting for Frieren to reappear again. The rain that the barrier had previously held back begins pouring down. Using the rain, Lawine and Kanne manage to easily overpower Richter with their magic, winning the battle. Later, after the Second Party has left with the Stille, the Thirteenth Party regroup, and despite being out of mana, they engage in a fist fight with another team and are able to secure a Stille. Various teams are shown in the final few hours of the exam defending or securing their Stille. At sunset, Genau declares the first exam to be over and reveals that six parties have passed the first stage of the exam. Meanwhile, Stark is shown having a drink in a bar. He comments that two days have passed since the First-Class Mage Exam's start.

chapters.title: An Even-Better Flavor
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Genau introduces the six parties that have passed the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. He then explains that the second stage of the exam will begin in three days and dismisses all the examinees. The next day, back in Äußerst, Stark wakes up in the evening. Fern chastises Stark and Frieren for their childish antics and they decide to take Fern to a nice restaurant in town to make up for angering her. Meanwhile, Richter is shown working in a shop and repairing items with magic. Denken and Laufen convince him to go to a restaurant with them, coincidentally the same one Frieren's Party have decided to go to. Meanwhile, Übel finds Land and starts a conversation with him. She reveals that she is able to learn others' magic through empathy; as a result, she wishes to get to know Land better. At the restaurant, Stark notes the exorbitant amount of food Frieren has ordered. Frieren recalls her memory of dining at this same restaurant with the Hero Party, where she explained that she must relish good food because it she so often will never have the chance to taste that same flavor again. In the present day, Frieren tries the food and comments that the taste has changed, but she smiles as she realizes it has become even better than before.

chapters.title: The Third Exam

Serie decides she will be in charge of the third exam. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Serie decides who passes and fails based on her instincts. She fails Kanne, Dünste, Laufen, Scharf, and Ehre because they cannot visualize becoming first-class mages, and Frieren due to their ongoing ideological dispute over magic. Frieren tells Serie she was only able to meet the Hero Party due to the flower field spell Serie finds foolish; she also tells Serie she will not be able to fail Fern. Serie speaks with the remaining candidates and passes Denken, Übel, Land, Wirbel, and Methode. Afterwards, the examinees gather outside the Continental Magic Association either celebrating or commiserating. Denken thanks Frieren for her help, as now he can visit his wife's grave in his hometown. The third stage of the First-Class Mage Exam concludes.

chapters.title: With a Little Help
chapters.summary:
After the conclusion of the First-Class Mage Exam, many examinees remain in Äußerst as they prepare for their next courses of action. Denken treats Laufen, Fern, and Stark to sweets, as his wife passed away when he was young and he has no one to spend his money on. He asks Fern to thank Frieren for reminding him of the joy of magic because Frieren was the one who inspired him to become a mage.
Meanwhile, Wirbel encounters Frieren, and they discuss Wirbel's motivations. Wirbel tells Frieren that the silly adventure stories about Himmel the Hero were what brought him this far, and Frieren recalls Himmel saying that he would not turn his back on people who need a little help even if such actions do not change the world. Frieren reckons that the world is changing after all. Fern later asks Stark and Frieren to attend the ceremony for the special privileges granted to the new first-class mages, but Frieren appears displeased at the thought.

chapters.title: Magic-Nullifying Crystal
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the death of Himmel the Hero, Frieren's Party is in the Saum Marshes. Frieren finds a Magic-Nullifying Crystal and tells Fern and Stark about its properties. Later, the ground collapses beneath them and they fall into a cave made of magic-nullifying crystal, which they trek through. Fern wonders how Frieren can sleep so soundly in their situation, as the crystals prevent them from using magic, and Fern admits to Stark that she is terrified. They are suddenly interrupted by a Venomous Apex Dragon bursting out of the water, and as they prepare to face it, Frieren tells Stark that she is able to sleep soundly because she has entrusted her life to him, and if he wants to flee, then they will flee together as they are a party, just as the Hero Party did. She pours mana into a magic-nullifying crystal and uses it to blind the dragon, and Frieren's party escapes from the cave together. They then continue on their travels north.

chapters.title: Why I Set Out on This Journey
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the death of the Hero Himmel, Frieren's Party is in the Great Sanft Forest. Stark accidentally walks to the river when Fern and Frieren are bathing, and the mood becomes tense. They arrive at a fork in the road between the Northern Plateau and Neutral Harbor. Inside the inn at the fork they encounter Wirbel, Ehre, and Scharf. Wirbel asks Frieren to let him convince Stark to help him in the war in the Northern Frontier for two or three years to stabilize the front. Frieren agrees, and states that perhaps Stark felt uncomfortable in their party. Later that evening, Fern approaches Stark who tells her that he turned Wirbel down and that he genuinely wanted to join Fern and Frieren, in large part because of Fern's encouragement. The next day, Wirbel's Party and Frieren's Party go their separate ways, with Wirbel stating they will meet again at the Northern Frontier sooner or later.

chapters.title: The Hero of the South
chapters.summary:
Twenty-nine years after the death of the Hero Himmel, Frieren's Party are in Fabel Village. They receive a request to polish a hero's statue. To Fern and Stark's surprise, it is not a statue of Himmel, but of the Hero of the South. Frieren explains the feats of the Hero of the South, who wiped out the Demon King's frontline forces, killed three of the Seven Sages of Destruction, and ultimately slayed Schlacht the Omniscient.
As they clean up his statue, Frieren recalls meeting the Hero of the South while she was living in the Central Lands. He is unable to convince her to join him, but he tells her his secret: he can actually see the future, and has foreseen he will die in a year. However, he tells Frieren that a young hero will visit her soon and that she will defeat the Demon King with him; he asks her to tell this hero that he, humanity's greatest hero, promises he will blaze a path to the future, even if he doesn't make a mark on history. Frieren finishes polishing his statue and thinks that he has, in fact, made his mark in history.

Graf Dach invites them to a banquet before they can leave, and request they retrieve an heirloom sword stolen by a demon. Frieren's Party head in the direction the demon fled, and after journeying, find a village in ruins with a lone priestess in the area. The priestess asks them to pray for the villagers with her, but Frieren blasts a grave and reveals no one is buried, because the villagers were eaten by the fake priestess, who is actually the demon with a sword. They defeat the demon and Frieren remembers Himmel declaring that he would never leave people in need, no matter how challenging the request. They return the sword to Graf Dach and continue on their travels.

chapters.title: The Secret Hot Spring of the Etwas Mountains
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Etwas Mountains. The temperature is warmer because they have reached a volcanic belt, and Fern is excited at the prospect of a hot spring. However, the village and hot springs that Frieren expects to find have been abandoned for 30 years, and the hot springs have dried up. The family in the cabin that tells them of this mentions there is a secret hot spring in the Etwas Mountains. Stark wants to check out the secret hot spring despite Frieren's insistence it's not worth the time and effort. They journey to the secret hot spring, defeating a three-headed lizard along the way, and find a shallow hot spring only suitable for a footbath. However, Stark points out it isn't bad, as it means they can all get in together and look at the view - the same one Eisen and the Hero Party had saw. Afterwards, they trek back to the main road from the hot spring.

chapters.title: The Places She Would Like
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Fortified City of Heiß. As they have some free time, Stark, in an attempt to get even with Fern's harshness, asks her on a date. To his surprise, she accepts. Stark then asks Frieren for advice on what Fern would like, and Frieren takes him to spots around the city she thinks Fern would enjoy. Stark comments that she knows Fern well, but Frieren says it is really Heiter who knew her well. Nonetheless, Stark says it is impressive for Frieren to remember all these things, and she is managing to be a good parent after all. The next morning, Fern asks Frieren which dress is better. A tired Frieren says they're the same, and Fern braids Frieren's hair angrily. After, Stark and Fern meet in the streets, and head out on their date.

chapters.title: Peaceful Time
chapters.summary: Right after the events of the previous chapter, Fern and Stark go on their date together. Stark takes Fern to all the places Frieren showed him, including a market, street food vendors, a statue of Himmel in the town plaza, a dessert place, and an overlook of the city. Stark comments that Fern isn't having much fun, as she hasn't smiled all day. Fern admits that while Stark took her to places she'd normally like, it didn't feel like places he would choose. Stark admits that he had Frieren pick all the spots, and while Fern admits that she is a little disappointed, she is happy he put so much thought into the date for her. Afterwards, they sit together and talk about their masters; later, Fern and Frieren sit in the hot springs together, and Frieren notes that Fern is in a good mood. The next day, they depart from the Fortified City of Heiß and continue on their travels, this time with Frieren's hair in good-mood braids.

chapters.title: Northern Plateau
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is in the Nachricht Region. They pass through the checkpoint to the Northern Plateau, and quickly encounter a variety of different monsters. They stop at a cabin, where a villager requests they subjugate a monster further up the road. Stark questions why the villagers don't leave for safer lands, but the villager says that this land is filled with his family's memories, and asks how one could abandon their hometown. After subjugating the monster, Stark wonders if going by sea would have been easier, but Frieren recalls Himmel saying he wants to protect other people's homes, not just his own, and she tells Stark that many people call the Northern Plateau home. Stark and Fern both agree, and the party then continues their travels.

chapters.title: Boshaft—The Emperor's Spirit
chapters.summary:
Twenty-nine years after the passing of Himmel the Hero, Frieren's Party arrives at a town in the Bier Region. They overhear that a Dwarf named Fass, who has been seeking the alcoholic drink Boshaft—said to be the finest spirit in the world—is close to finding it after searching for two centuries. Fass asks for Frieren's assistance, as he has found the ruins Boshaft is stored in based on a stone tablet in Ancient Elvish and needs help breaking the barrier spell over the door.
Frieren ends up deciphering the barrier after three months, but she is unhappy as she knows the truth behind the alcohol, which the elf Milliarde, despondent after spending her whole life pursuing something worthless, had hid for no reason. Frieren worries the same fate will befall Fass, but upon finally trying Boshaft, Fass laughs in delight and makes the whole town try it. Fass tells them that although the drink was disappointing, he is glad that they were there, as he has never had such a fun night.

chapters.title: Divine Revolte
chapters.summary: Stark returns to the campfire and shares a late-night snack with Genau, who identifies the demon that attacked the village as the Divine Revolte, the same demon who killed his former partner. When Revolte appears, he immediately attacks them. Genau uses the spell to manipulate niello wings: Digardnacht to block Revolte's blows and warns Stark not to take the attacks head-on, but Stark is still struck, creating an opening for Genau to wound Revolte. Revolte recognizes Genau and taunts him about his dead comrade, then tricks him by using a demon disguised as a child to exploit human instincts to protect children. Although Genau is stabbed in the torso, he quickly recovers and kills the disguised demon, realizing his judgment had been clouded by memories of his fallen partner. Revolte moves to finish Genau, but Stark blocks him, refusing to stay down. As Stark insists that the last person standing wins, Genau agrees and decides to keep fighting alongside him.

The ferryman offers a request to find the Hero Himmel's lost memoir in lieu of payment, and Frieren accepts. After dismantling the barrier protecting the abandoned monastery where the memoir was rumored to be, Frieren locates the memoir and offers it to the ferryman. chapters.title: The Golden Land
chapters.summary: Thirty years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party are in the Weise Region. Frieren's Party receives a private request from first-class mage Lernen to assist the new barrier keeper of the Golden Land, which is a region transformed into gold at the hands of Macht, one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, fifty years ago. Frieren is initially wary but accepts due to a grimoire that is included as the reward. Upon arriving at the Golden Land, they find that the new keeper of the Golden Land's barrier is Denken, who finally receives the post after successfully becoming a first-class mage. Denken, having revisited his hometown, intends to face Macht of Golden Land and return the Golden Land to normal, an idea which Frieren immediately dismisses as she refuses to engage in a battle with Macht. It turns out that Macht is one of the eleven people Frieren has lost to, and she can still not picture herself defeating Macht. Frieren says it is the best choice to leave him sealed inside the barrier until he dies, to which Denken says that was his initial idea. However, after he revisited his hometown and visited his wife's grave, he decided on this undertaking. Denken tells Frieren's Party they do not have to accept the request and that he intends to face Macht alone, but Frieren, after recalling a memory with Himmel and the Hero Party, agrees to help Denken "seize a chance of victory."

chapters.title: Diagoldze—The Spell to Transmute All Creation into Gold
chapters.summary:
Denken invites Frieren's Party into the hut prepared for the barrier keepers, explaining that barely anyone uses it. Frieren remarks it is because the Golden Land and Macht naturally makes mages nervous. Fern is also anxious and explains that even though the Golden Land is such a huge region magically turned into gold, she cannot feel any mana coming from it. She says that the Golden Land is detected as a mass of pure, solid gold instead of magic. Frieren talks about Macht's specialized magic, the spell to transmute all creation into gold: Diagoldze - an irreversible curse which is imperceptible as magic. It is because of this unique power that Macht is considered the most powerful Sage of Destruction. She concludes that it is impossible to counter his magic and says that Serie's presence is required. Denken begins to tell them about the information he gathered, but Frieren asks him to start from the conclusion. Denken then says if they start from the conclusion, then the conclusion is that it is impossible to defeat Macht.
Meanwhile, first-class mage Lernen and second-class mage Edel are on a wagon. Edel, seeming exhausted, asks Lernen why he went to great lengths to assist Denken. Lernen reveals that they are old friends and were fellow Imperial Mages. When Lernen was expelled from his position, Denken was the only person who defended him until the end, which made Lernen feel indebted. Yet, through many years, like Denken delaying his return to his hometown, Lernen delayed repaying Denken. Therefore, when Denken finally decided to return, Lernen also decided to help him. Edel comments that it was too late, to which Lernen agrees, saying "There is no such thing as "someday" in our lives," and that they should have realized sooner.

chapters.title: Stone Bracelet of Servitude
chapters.summary:
Denken details the investigation Lernen had launched into the Golden Land, after mentioning that he had entered the Golden Land and left unscathed even after being found by Macht. Lernen recruits second-class mage Edel with him on his quest to investigate the Golden Land, to which Edel reluctantly agrees, while citing that she cannot possibly investigate a demon. He presents her with the replica of the Stone Bracelet of Servitude, the only magical item that is capable of controlling a demon's mind. Apparently, the ruler of the Fortress City of Weise used the Stone Bracelet of Servitude to freely control Macht, until the demon resisted and transmuted the whole city into gold. He informs Edel that Macht of Golden Land was rumored to still be wearing the bracelet and asked her to study its enchantment in an attempt to restore the bracelet. 
Afterwards, they travel to the area outside the Golden Land where they encounter second-class mage Früh, who was part of the party of mages Lernen had asked to conduct a preliminary examination in the Golden Land. Fruh told them that their party encountered Macht inside the Golden Land and was wiped out in the blink of an eye. Lernen then asks why she was able to escape, or why Macht had let her flee. Before she can form a reply, Früh is transmuted into gold so quickly that Edel cannot read her memory. Lernen states that Macht probably delayed her transformation as a warning to outsiders and that they had underestimated Macht.

chapters.summary:
Before entering the Golden Land, Lernen leads Edel to meet one of the last remaining survivors of the Fortress City of Weise, who was a servant of the Glück family. He has given permission for Edel to read his memories in the hopes of gathering information on Macht. Edel reads the memory of the feudal lord putting the Stone Bracelet of Servitude on Macht and retells that the lord ordered Macht not to "hold malice towards the people of Weise."
As they enter the Golden Land, Edel remarks how the situation was peculiar, since the gold made from Macht's magic is indestructible and thus cannot be refined, it has no real value and thus contradicts the theory that the lord's wish was to gain unfathomable riches. When they enter the city, they are quickly discovered by Macht, who says they should have turned back and that because they did not, he has to kill them and make an example for others. Before Macht can launch his attack, Lernen has made his own, telling him that he has never been praised so remarkably.

chapters.title: Malice
chapters.summary: Right after First-Class Mage Lernen fires a shot at Macht, Lernen and Macht begin to fight as Second-Class Mage Edel attempts to restore the Stone Bracelet of Servitude. Macht notices that Lernen is only attempting to stall, and not to kill, and questions Lernen as to what his true objective is. Edel informs Lernen that there is no issue with the bracelet, and that everything is working as intended. When Lernen asks how Macht could have turned the city to gold without any malice, Macht tells Lernen that demons do not have any concept of malice, and cannot harbor any in the first place. Lernen decides to retreat to return in the future and summons a golem, but Macht attempts to stop them from retreating, slashing through the golem and wounding Lernen. Edel rushes up outside of Macht's view, briefly touching him and reading his memories. Macht is surprised that she managed to do so, and Lernen congratulates Edel on her work and summons a massive golem. Macht transmutes the golem to gold as it swings its sword, but loses Lernen and Edel in the resulting smoke.

chapters.title: Discussions
chapters.summary:
Denken reveals that he has been able to enter and leave the Golden Land as well as converse with Macht because he is a citizen of the Fortress City of Weise, thereby binding Macht to "serve" him. As a result, Macht presumably cannot kill him. When asked why he persists with meaningless talks, Denken explains it is because he wants to return the Golden Land to normal. Since Macht's magic remains even after he perishes, Denken cannot kill him even if he managed to find a way to do so. Frieren then asks to join the talks, saying she wants to confirm something by seeing Macht face-to-face.
The four of them go to see Macht inside the Fortress City of Weise. Frieren tries to instigate a fight with Macht upon meeting him again, but Denken stops Macht from escalating. Afterwards, Macht serves them tea and they have a brief conversation. However, when questioned why he keeps killing people even though he wants to coexist, Macht seems confused as to the point of the question, which leads Frieren to conclude they will never be able to understand each other. As they leave, Frieren asks Denken about the relationship between him and Macht. Denken replies that Macht used to be his magic teacher.

chapters.title: Affection
chapters.summary:
Back at the keeper's hut, Denken fills the others in on the history between him and Macht. He says that Macht had begun serving the feudal lord eighty years ago and was only equipped with the Stone Bracelet of Servitude twenty years after. However, it was not the Bracelet that made him benign; during his servitude he had never once disobeyed Lord Glück's orders. Denken then asks Frieren whether she had found a clue to defeating Macht from the talk, but Frieren seems to evade the question, saying that she does not have enough confidence to call it a chance of victory. She then asks Denken about the details of Macht's memories. Denken replies that he has not finished analyzing the memories due to the fact they cover up to a hundred years ago. Having heard this, Frieren agrees to help Denken analyze and read the memories together.
Meanwhile in the Golden Land, Macht ponders to himself about the difference in sensibilities between humans and demons and predicts that Frieren will see his memories. He expresses the wish to "engage in battle" with her "for the sake of coexistence" and to find the answer he has been looking for there. 
In Macht's recollections, he is in the midst of destroying a human village when he encounters a priest who recognizes that he doesn't experience emotions of malice or guilt and expresses pity for him. After killing the priest, he begins having doubts about the emotions which humans possess but demons like him lack. This is the beginning of his journey to attempt to understand human emotions and find a path for coexistence.

chapters.title: Solitär
chapters.summary:
Macht's recollection continues at the scene of another village being massacred. There he encounters Wahrheit, one of the members of the Three Great Knightly Families of the Northern Lands. Wahrheit begins attacking Macht despite the demon's warning. Initially, Macht engages in combat with him. However, once Wahrheit states that through examining Macht's previous massacres he has concluded that there must be some complicated activation mechanism to his special magic, Macht unceremoniously ends the battle, turning the knight into gold without any trouble.
Afterwards, Macht meets up with an eccentric demon who engages in research on human beings, whose name is Solitär. She leads him back to her lodging and shows him the skeletal remains from a shark and an orca. She explains to him the concept of "Convergent Evolution." When Macht asks her about the human emotions which demons lacked, Solitär tells him the reason is because the demons evolved to prey on humans. Even though they have similar appearances and behaviors, they are entirely different creatures, thus they will never be able to understand each other. In response, Macht tells her that demons might be able to coexist with humans if they are able to understand their emotions, and that demons like him have more than enough time to waste. 
Afterwards, Macht sits by himself at the site of another settlement he destroyed. He is visited by Schlacht the Omniscient, who asks for his assistance in the battle to take down the Hero of the South.

chapters.title: Guilt
chapters.summary:
Macht initially refuses to participate in the battle at Schlacht's behest. However, Schlacht tells him that it is an order from the Demon King and threatens to kill Macht if he disobeys. After testing the waters, Macht concurs, noting that Schlacht has brought with him the Magnificient Grausam, an opponent he has the worst matchup against. He asks Schlacht for more instructions and is told he simply needs to be present to fight. Schlacht informs Macht that he will erase his memories of the battle because he will let his memory be read by another in the future. Through Macht, Schlacht addresses Frieren, predicting that she will eventually come upon Macht's memories. 
The scene shifts to years later, where Macht has killed countless people without any particular reason but to attempt to feel malice or guilt. He watches a childhood friend kill the other, having promised them he would let the survivor live. Upon seeing the scene, Macht comes to a new realization: he cannot feel anything because he knows nothing about the people he kills. He wonders if he would be able to understand such emotions if he killed someone close to him, and sets out with a new goal in mind to find people who could be called "close" to him.
